detail: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's page on Hong Kong notes states: "Banknotes issued by the note-issuing banks are printed in Hong Kong by Hong Kong Note Printing Limited (HKNPL)." The same page states that "The Government continues to exercise management control and maintains a majority stake in HKNPL, with the Chief Executive of the HKMA as the Chairman of the company."
source_title: Hong Kong Currency - Notes (Hong Kong Monetary Authority)

detail: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing's own About page states: "The BEP prints billions of dollars – referred to as Federal Reserve notes – each year." The page gives no location for the agency.

An interview with the Bank of Mauritius published on the Bank's own website (a Currency News special issue for the Banknote 2014 conference) states that the Rs25 and Rs50 notes were supplied by Oberthur. The document says "supplied by" rather than "printed by", and gives no contract value and no indication of the position after 2014.
source_title: Putting the 'Swing' into the New Mauritius Notes (Bank of Mauritius communique)

detail: An interview with the Bank of Mauritius published on the Bank's own website (a Currency News special issue for the Banknote 2014 conference) refers to "the Rs500 note supplied by De La Rue". The document says "supplied by" rather than "printed by", and gives no contract value and no indication of the position after 2014.
source_title: Putting the 'Swing' into the New Mauritius Notes (Bank of Mauritius communique)

detail: PWPW's own news page states that it signed a contract with the Central Bank of Paraguay for "the production and delivery of 28 million banknotes of two denominations: 10 000 and 20 000 guarani". A separate PWPW news page on a delivery of 35 tons of banknotes refers to "Representatives of our customer, that is the Central Bank of Paraguay" and to the bank's vault in Asuncion; that second page gives no date. No contract value is given on either page.
source_title: More banknotes from Poland for Paraguay (PWPW)

detail: PWPW's own news page on its 2018 export results states that PWPW produced "55 million banknotes for the Dominican Republic", and lists "banknote contracts for Honduras, Paraguay and the Dominican Republic" among its successes. The page names no Dominican counterparty, gives no contract value, and states that "Most of PWPW contracts are secret."
source_title: The value of PWPW exports doubled in 2018 (PWPW)

detail: A Detik Finance report of 13 December 2022 states that Peruri has secured an order to print banknotes for Peru, calling Peru "pasar paling baru yang berhasil ditembus Peruri" (the newest market Peruri has successfully entered); it names no Peruvian counterparty and gives no contract value. An earlier Detik report of 8 January 2020 said Peruri had won the tender to print the 10, 20 and 50 nuevo sol denominations, with the contract then still to be signed.
source_title: Top! RI Cetak Duit buat Peru hingga Nepal, Kini Incar Argentina (Detik Finance)

detail: A De La Rue press release headed "The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue" states that the series was "originated and produced by De La Rue", covering the 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 leke denominations, with the 200 and 5000 leke entering circulation "from 30 September" and the rest over the following three years. No year and no contract value are given on the page.
source_title: The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue (press release)

detail: On a G+D page carrying an interview with the Central Bank of Armenia about its third banknote series, the Bank's representative answers the question "How did you select the banknote printer?" by saying "Giesecke+Devrient won as a result of a comprehensive evaluation of all offers." The page does not state in so many words that G+D printed the notes, and gives no contract value. Its dating is inconsistent: it is labelled "Published in Currency News June 2019" while the interview refers to the series being introduced "at the start of this year" and the page's meta description says the start of 2021.
as_of: page labelled "Published in Currency News June 2019"
source_title: Armenia - optimising its new series through design, security and substrate (Giesecke+Devrient)

name_as_stated: STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA
detail: The Czech National Bank's description of its commemorative banknote marking the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency (Karel Englis) states that the reverse bears, in tiny letters near the lower edge, the inscription "STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA". The page states no printing date; the note's year of issue is 2022 and it entered circulation on 30 March 2022. The page does not say who prints the Czech National Bank's circulating banknotes.
source_title: Commemorative banknote featuring a motif on the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency (Czech National Bank)
